Claim 105210 includes primary diagnosis O99.013 (Anemia complicating pregnancy, third trimester) which is a maternity ICD code. The grid maternity flag was not set in the submitted claim.

thynk_response.shortMessage: Unspecified anemia code D64.9 should be replaced with specific anemia type when maternity/pregnancy diagnosis O99.013 is billed.
thynk_response.longMessage: When O99.013 (Anemia complicating pregnancy, third trimester) is coded, generic unspecified code D64.9 is inappropriate without specifying the anemia type. Given that E83.42 (Hypomagnesaemia) is also present as a secondary diagnosis, consider whether the anemia is related to nutritional deficiency (D50.9 iron deficiency, D51.9 B12 deficiency, or D52.9 folate deficiency) and replace D64.9 with the clinically appropriate specific code.

thynk_response.shortMessage: Multiple iron study lab tests billed concurrently (82728 Ferritin, 83540 Iron, 83550 Iron Binding Capacity).
thynk_response.longMessage: CPT codes 82728 (Ferritin), 83540 (Iron serum), and 83550 (Iron binding capacity) are all billed in the same encounter. These three tests together form a complete iron panel and payer bundling guidelines may require they be submitted as a panel rather than individually. Verify against the applicable DoH/DHA fee schedule and bundling rules. The iron panel is clinically supported by the secondary diagnosis D64.9 (anemia) and maternity diagnosis O99.013.

thynk_response.shortMessage: TSH test (84443) medical necessity requires thyroid-related diagnosis alongside maternity complication.
thynk_response.longMessage: CPT 84443 (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) is billed under primary diagnosis O99.013 (Anemia complicating pregnancy, third trimester). While R00.2 (Palpitations) is present as a secondary diagnosis which can indicate thyroid dysfunction, a specific thyroid diagnosis (E03.9 Hypothyroidism, E05.90 Hyperthyroidism) would strengthen medical necessity. Palpitations in pregnancy with anemia can be cardiac or thyroid in origin — if thyroid pathology is confirmed, add the specific thyroid ICD code to fully justify 84443.
